title: Beyond the Village Wall
story:
After days spent inside the quiet warmth of the shed and working alongside Don Tadeo, James felt the undeniable tug of the horizon once more. The rhythm of sanding cedar and fitting chapel frames had restored his spirits, but his gaze kept returning to the weathered stone archway of Aldea San Gabriel’s southern perimeter wall. Beyond that boundary lay the open wildness of the highland valley—rolling hills of sun-dried amber grass, wild agave, and ancient stone ruins standing under a wide, cloudless sky.

He had known the dense, damp shade of the Great Canopy. He had known the misty cobblestones of Oakhaven. He had known the peaceful comfort of Don Tadeo’s carpentry shop. But he had not yet walked the wide, dry trails of the southern plains. With his leather strap adjusted across his shoulder and his brass map canister resting comfortably at his hip, James bade a silent farewell to the quiet village lanes and stepped through the cracked perimeter gate.

The path beyond the wall was a narrow dirt track carved through golden scrubland, smelling rich with sunburnt sage and warm earth. Climbing to a high limestone outcropping that overlooked a dry riverbed, James paused to catch his breath. He drew out his small brass compass, watching the slender needle tremble before settling decisively toward the south. Resting one palm against the warm limestone, he offered his familiar, quiet greeting to the expansive landscape: "Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next."

From his high perch, James retrieved his smooth piece of green sea-glass and held it to his eye. Through the tinted glass, the sweeping yellow valley transformed into a vast emerald sea, waving gently beneath the highland breeze. Below him in the gulley, half-draped in wild flowering vines, lay the mossy remnants of an ancient stone highway marker, proving that travelers had journeyed down this trail long before him.

James sat on the sunlit ledge, his tail curled neatly around his paws as the shadow of a passing red-tailed hawk glided across the valley floor. He reached into a rock crevice to pluck a small sprig of fragrant wild sage, tucking it carefully into his leather strap alongside Mateo’s woven threads. Behind him, Aldea San Gabriel looked small and peaceful, cradled by the northern hills; ahead of him, the southern world stretched wide and bright under the sun.
